title: L&T Profit Jumps 33% to Rs 5,202 Crore on Record Order Inflow
excerpt: Larsen & Toubro's second-quarter profit rose 33% to Rs 5,202 crore as revenue grew 16%, but a flat EBITDA squeezed margins to 8.7% — a scale-versus-profitability split investors will weigh against a record Rs 1.47 lakh crore order intake.
body:
• Larsen & Toubro reported consolidated net profit of Rs 5,202 crore for Q2 FY27, up 33% from Rs 3,926 crore a year earlier.
  • Revenue from operations rose 16% to Rs 78,750 crore, driven by its Projects, Products & Manufacturing portfolio, with international revenue at Rs 45,870 crore — 58% of the total.
  • Order intake hit a record Rs 1.47 lakh crore, up 28% year on year, with international contracts making up the majority of new orders.
  • EBITDA was broadly flat at Rs 6,845 crore, pulling the margin down to about 8.7% from 10.0% a year ago — the one soft spot in the quarter.

Larsen & Toubro reported a 33% rise in second-quarter net profit on Tuesday, buoyed by healthy order inflows amid strong infrastructure spending and reconstruction activity in the Middle East, even as the engineering major cautioned that inflation and geopolitical risks continue to cloud the global outlook.

Consolidated net profit for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was Rs 5,202 crore, against Rs 3,926 crore in the same period a year earlier, according to the company's results reported by The Hindu BusinessLine. Revenue from operations grew 16% to Rs 78,750 crore from Rs 67,984 crore. Lower finance costs, treasury income and working-capital efficiency also contributed to the profit gain.

Record orders, international weight

Order intake grew 28% year on year to Rs 1.47 lakh crore — L&T's highest ever quarterly inflow — with over half of new contracts coming from the hydrocarbon and offshore energy business and the bulk of those energy orders from international markets. International revenue during the quarter was Rs 45,870 crore, constituting 58% of total revenue.

"The company has delivered a strong quarter in an ever-changing geopolitical landscape. This performance reflects continued customer confidence and our ability to secure large and complex orders across sectors and geographies."

— S. N. Subrahmanyan, Chairman and Managing Director, L&T

The margin question

The quarter's tension sits in profitability per rupee of work. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation were largely flat at Rs 6,845 crore, so the margin contracted to about 8.7% from 10.0% a year earlier as revenue mix shifted toward large project work. Analysts tracking the stock will weigh that compression against the visibility a record order book provides.

L&T President and Whole-time Director (Finance) R. Shankar Raman said project opportunities worth Rs 10 lakh crore are visible across domestic and international markets and that the company remains optimistic about maintaining its order-win run rate in the second half. The one sector facing execution challenges is water supply, where projects worth Rs 40,000 crore face funding delays from state governments, he said.

Outlook

In its outlook, the company said India's macroeconomic fundamentals remained resilient despite trade tensions, geopolitical conflicts and high energy prices, while inflation — from food price volatility, elevated energy costs and weather disruption — remains a concern. Ahead of the results, L&T shares closed 0.40% lower at Rs 3,665.10 on the NSE on Tuesday. For investors, the next two quarters will show whether the record inflow converts to revenue without further margin dilution.
